text: We evaluated weak-to-strong generalization via bootstrapping through an intermediate-size model, using gpt2-medium as the weak supervisor, pythia-1b as the intermediate step, and mistral-7b as the strong student, across 10 seeds. The weak supervisor reached 0.47 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.70, while the bootstrapped transfer model attained 0.49 accuracy with a standard error of 0.02. The resulting performance gap recovered (PGR) was 0.08 with a standard error of 0.10, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.14. The bootstrapped pipeline therefore did not outperform the baseline; its PGR point estimate sits below the baseline, and the large standard error on PGR means the data cannot distinguish the two approaches in either direction. Readers should note that the PGR standard error is comparable in magnitude to the PGR estimate itself, so no directional conclusion about the benefit of the intermediate model is supported here.
